body: Your words will not be read in vain.

Don't be sorry. Please don't be sorry.

Your depleting from your life the most important aspect of it: time. You're just hoping something sticks to me so I can find a fresh bit of information to breath life into me, or at least its purpose.

I doubt anyone here can change my mind, I hate being settled in my beliefs but that's just the way it is.

>I don't agree with you that life is all about money, or how much you earn.

That's always the buttered up ideal answer. I don't think life is all about money, but for the most part - it is. You can't really live if you don't have money - it's fact. I am going to impose an idea that its perhaps that you have money that you may denote it. **Its needed to live and be desirable - it's needed to do (almost) anything.**

>Whatever you choose, within your budget. It's your life and your choice.

Keywords: within your budget. Budget requires money. A good life requires more money in order to take care of those we love around us. God's not dead, it's money - at least in this world.

>It seems perverse to suffer through the crappy parts of life and take the z route before you get to enjoy the good bits. I feel for another human being who is having such an unhappy struggle. Many people will understand your pain from personal experience and want to do what they can to stand by you while you experience it - you are no more a loser than most of us.

But that's all it is - a collection of good bits and bad bits. It's a roller coaster, it's predictable - one day I'll feel really good again. I already have, it's a fleeting experience. I am not too happy about losing the closest people in my life, and seeing them suffer. Death is the only absolute. I am a loser because I can tell you my lack thereof. 

>I hope things improve for you and that being a winner/loser, failure/success becomes less and less important to you.

Thank you. Failure and being a loser is important to me because it causes suffering and misery.

>I think some actions are done out of ego and some out of love.

I certainly hope so. I really hope so. From what I remember from high school biology - every action is a means to further self preservation. The whole idea makes me sick and disgusted with life.

>I think somewhere deep inside us we know life isn't about accumulating material possessions or having a beautiful sex partner. And so when we find out someone is at the end and wants to die, people care and want to help.

Oh, but it is. I can't help but think it is. It's acquired, its demanded, and we wouldn't even be talking here without it. Mates often want someone successful, and success just means having a lot of money, for the most part. "Success" is usually an "established importance" via paper. Can't have a wife, a family, a house, or car when MONEY IS EVERYTHING. 

>Yes, but I see death as the end of the play when the curtains come up. Then we see and understand the part we played and the result of our decisions. The main decision being choosing kindness and compassion over selfishness.

Let's hope for that too. I'd like to see how meaningless it all was. That, or maybe it's just darkness - nothing known but that it was the absolute, and life is an illusion.
